overview: Rise 6.2.4's KillAura is the successor of the 5.99 Aura, rebuilt on the event bus and the shared RotationComponent. It keeps Single, Switch and Multiple attack modes plus Distance/Health/Hurt Time sorting, and expands the bypass surface to fifteen auto-block modes (None, Fake, Vanilla, NCP, Legit, Grim, Intave, Old Intave, Imperfect Vanilla, Vanilla ReBlock, Watchdog 1.17, New NCP, Universal, Watchdog, Watchdog 2), four rotation modes (Legit/Normal, Snap, NCP, Autistic AntiCheat), click-delay modes including 1.9+ weapon-speed scaling, a cps bounds randomization, an EvictingList of past targets for Switch mode, and heavy use of the component system: TargetComponent for target acquisition, RotationComponent for smoothed rotations with a ray-cast predicate, PingSpoofComponent for the Universal/Watchdog block cycles, and BadPacketsComponent to suppress attacks while movement is desynced.

sections.p: The module is event-driven with priority-ordered listeners. onHighPreUpdate (Priorities.HIGH) is the target and rotation pass: it refreshes the mouse over, computes allowAttack from BadPacketsComponent, calls getTargets() (which delegates to TargetComponent.getTargets(range) and applies the Switch-mode pastTargets eviction plus expandRange heuristics), picks targets.get(0), runs preBlock() for the auto-block mode, then rotations(). onMediumPriorityPreUpdate runs after other modules have had their chance to override rotations, and only then calls doAttack(targets) and postAttackBlock(), so the module attacks with the final rotation state. onPreMotionEvent flushes the packetQueue (packets queued by the blink/ping-spoof modes) via sendNoEvent, increments hitTicks, and clears blocking when the held item is not a sword. onPostMotion sends the block packet. onPacketSend tracks swing state (C0A sets swing=true, C03 resets it) and dispatches the Intave packetBlock mode, which cancels the outgoing C03, unblocks, re-sends the C03 without events, and re-blocks.

rotations() switches on rotationMode. Legit/Normal computes the target rotations with RotationUtil.calculate(target, true, range) and feeds RotationComponent.setRotations with a randomized rotationSpeed from the bounds setting plus a ray-cast predicate: the smoothing loop keeps jittering the target rotations with a random-angle offset (speed = random^3 * 20, offset accumulated via sin/cos of randomAngle) until RayCastUtil.rayCast(rotations, range, -0.1) hits an entity, which keeps every interpolated rotation inside the target's hitbox. NCP mode predicts both the target's position (MoveUtil.predictMovement) and the player's own motion, computes the axis via applySensitivityPatch, and with 10% probability adds a random offset of up to 10 yaw / 3 pitch. Snap mode only applies rotations when lastSafeUnBlockTick() allows, otherwise keeps the current rotations. doAttack() gates on the attackStopWatch/clickStopWatch pair and cps.getRandomBetween() * 1.5, then attacks: with keepSprint it sends C02PacketUseEntity directly, otherwise mc.playerController.attackEntity; Single/Switch also fall through to attack the ray-cast entity when it is not a fireball or item frame, and Multiple attacks every target still within range in one tick.

The autoBlock value selects among fifteen sequences in preBlock()/postBlock()/postAttackBlock()/clickDelayBlock(). Grim and Watchdog 1.17 send a C09 held-item change to a different slot and back before blocking, which desyncs the server's view of the held item while the client still renders the sword. New NCP and Old Intave do the same C09 pair while the sword is blocked to mask the block state. Universal cycles blockTicks 2-3: block on tick 2, unblock on tick 3, with PingSpoofComponent.spoof(99999, ...) inflating the transaction ping during the cycle and dispatch() releasing the buffered packets at the right tick; Watchdog does the same with a random slot id sent every second tick, and Watchdog 2 adds a C09 to a random slot every third tick. clickDelayBlock() returns a 500ms penalty delay for Universal (blockTicks < 4) and Watchdog 1/2 (blockTicks < 2/1), so the module refuses to attack until the block cycle completes. The Fake and None modes cancel the RightClickEvent so the server never sees a use-item, and onRenderItem forces the EnumAction.BLOCK render so the client shows a blocking animation without any packet.

files.label: KillAura.java (module logic)
files.explanation: The 1057-line module file contains everything: the fifteen autoBlock submode values, the four rotation modes, the click-delay calculator (getDelay() scales the attack interval by weapon material: 1.6 speed for swords, 1.0 for spades, per-material axe/hoe speeds, computed as 1/speed*20-1 ticks), the target pipeline (getTargets() with the pastTargets EvictingList of size 9 so Switch mode never re-attacks a recently hit target, and the expandRange heuristic that every 20 ticks sets a random 3-3.5 block range expansion when no targets are found), the attack gate (doAttack() requires attackStopWatch.finished(nextSwing), clickStopWatch.finished(delay*50) or the Hit Select flag, and allowAttack from BadPacketsComponent unless badPacketsCheck is off), and the attack dispatch (keepSprint sends C02PacketUseEntity with syncCurrentPlayItem, otherwise playerController.attackEntity; Single/Switch attack the ray-cast entity when the primary target is out of range and the ray hits something that is not a fireball or item frame; Multiple removes out-of-range targets and attacks the rest). The block/ unblock pair sends C08 block placement and C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM, and the Grim/Watchdog modes emit the C09 slot-swap pairs. The packetQueue (ConcurrentLinkedQueue) is flushed at the top of onPreMotionEvent, which is how the Universal and Watchdog modes order their spoofed packets relative to the tick boundary.

files.label: RotationComponent.java (shared rotation engine)
files.explanation: KillAura drives all its aiming through this component. setRotations(targetRotations, rotationSpeed, correctMovement, raycast) stores the target, multiplies the speed by 36, and calls smooth(). smooth() is where the anti-detection work happens: when the target differs from the current rotations by more than 5 degrees it generates a random-angle walk (speed = (random*random*random)*20, offset incremented by sin/cos of a randomAngle that flips sign every 10 ticks) and offsets the target; after each offset it applies the raycast predicate supplied by the module, and if the offset misses the entity it inverts the walk direction and retries, finally falling back to targetRotations plus 2 degrees of jitter. This keeps every intermediate rotation on a curved path that still crosses the target hitbox, which defeats checks that only sample the final look while preserving aim. The component's onPreMotionEvent listener writes the smoothed rotations into the outgoing motion event (event.setYaw/Pitch), sets rotationYawHead and renderPitchHead, and records lastServerRotations, while LookEvent, StrafeEvent, MoveInputEvent and JumpEvent apply the movement fix when MovementFix is enabled. correctDisabledRotations() uses RotationUtil.resetRotation and applySensitivityPatch to snap the view back onto the GCD grid when the aura releases the look.

files.label: TargetComponent.java (entity acquisition)
files.explanation: KillAura.getTargets() delegates to TargetComponent.getTargets(range), which streams mc.theWorld.loadedEntityList and filters EntityLivingBase entries by the module's own BooleanValues: the player/invisibles/animals/mobs toggles (invisibles defaults false so invisible players are skipped), teams via PlayerUtil.sameTeam, friends via UserFriendAndTargetComponent, the bot manager blacklist, and armor stands excluded outright. The result is filtered by getDistanceToEntity <= range. The component holds a static reference to the KillAura module instance so the toggles can be read without wiring, and the same filter is shared by other combat modules (KeepRange, TickBase, Mimic) which is why the friend/bot/team logic lives here rather than in the module. For the KillAura this component is the full target-selection surface: the module only adds the Switch-mode pastTargets eviction, the expandRange retry, and the sort order on top of the component's distance-filtered list.

files.label: RotationUtil.java (rotation calculation and sensitivity patch)
files.explanation: The KillAura calls RotationUtil.calculate(target, true, range) in the Legit/Normal and Snap modes to get the exact yaw/pitch that points at the target's eyes, and RotationUtil.applySensitivityPatch in the NCP mode. calculate() returns the atan2-based look to the entity's position plus eye height, with the range parameter used to clamp the vertical delta. applySensitivityPatch is the 6.2.4 equivalent of the 5.99 getFixedRotation: it rounds the rotation delta to the mouse-sensitivity GCD (gcd = (sensitivity*0.6+0.2)^3 * 1.2) so the yaw/pitch stream sent to the server only contains deltas a real mouse could produce, which is what keeps the module's rotations from tripping rotation-snapping heuristics. The module's NCP rotation mode applies the patch after predicting both entities' motion, and the Legit/Normal mode feeds the unpatched result into RotationComponent where the smoothing walk runs. The utility also carries the resetRotation helper used by RotationComponent.correctDisabledRotations to return the view to the player's real rotations on the GCD grid when the aura stops aiming.

countering.label: Reach (lag-compensated ray trace with hitbox result)
countering.explanation: Grim's Reach is a two-phase check. On the ATTACK or INTERACT_ENTITY packet it queues the player's position with the entity id (onInteract), and on the next look/movement update (tickBetterReachCheckWithAngle) it runs the precise pass: for each possible look direction (current yaw/pitch, lastYaw/pitch for 1.8+ clients because 1.8 sends the attack a tick before the yaw, plus the 1.9 skipped-tick case) and each possible eye height, it casts a ray from the player's position and intersects the packet-entity's collision box; the minimum intercept distance is compared to the reach limit, which for pre-1.9 clients includes the 0.1 hitbox margin plus the movement threshold. A miss with no intersection returns the HITBOX result (routed to the Hitboxes check), and a distance over the limit returns REACH; cancelBuffer then aggressively cancels the next four attacks. KillAura's range setting goes to 6, so every attack beyond the vanilla 3.0-3.1 limit flags the REACH branch the instant the tick-end pass runs. The Multiple mode is hit twice: targets beyond range are removed client-side but the attack packet for each survivor is still measured, and any edge attack whose ray barely clips the box is measured against the limit. The Legit/Normal smoothing walk cannot help because Grim tests the actual look vectors against the server-tracked hitbox, and the module's C09 slot-swap block tricks do not alter the measured distance. On 1.8 servers the USE_1_8_HITBOX_MARGIN flag also mirrors the client-side 0.1 box expansion the module's own distance math relies on, so the client and Grim agree on the geometry and only the true distance decides.

countering.label: fight.Reach (survival distance with precision inset)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight.Reach measures the attack from the server-tracked player position to the victim and compares against reachSurvivalDistance (default 3.0). The check refines the victim y to the eye-height band, subtracts the getinset precision correction (half the victim width projected along the attack direction) when reachPrecision is on, and adds a per-entity size modifier (6.5 for dragons, 1.5 for giants). A positive violation accumulates into reachVL and executes the configured actions; the dynamic reachMod adaption then tightens the limit for repeat offenders: every hit within the reduce band steps reachMod down toward distanceMin, so a KillAura that consistently attacks at 3.1-3.4 gets silently cancelled even though the nominal limit is 3.0 plus inset. KillAura's range value of 3-6 maps directly onto this: the default 3.0 setting is near the limit and the higher settings exceed it outright. The module's client-side distance math subtracts nothing for the victim girth while NCP's inset grants only the half-width, so the server-side measurement is stricter than the client's own gate, and the 6.2.4 C04-less design (unlike the 5.99 Extended Range mode) means the server position cannot be shortened to dodge the measurement.

countering.label: fight.Angle (multi-target stream analysis)
countering.explanation: NCP's Angle check scores the attack stream for forcefield behavior. Every C02 appends an AttackLocation with the player position, yaw, victim id and timestamps, kept for maxTimeDiff (1000ms), and the window yields four averages: avgmove (distance moved between attacks, flagged under 0.2 blocks), avgtime (elapsed time between attacks, flagged under 150ms), avgyaw (total yaw change, flagged over 50 degrees), and switchspeed (victim id changes where the yaw diff exceeds 30 degrees). KillAura's Multiple mode attacks every in-range target from the same position in the same tick, which produces avgmove near zero, avgtime near zero, and a switchspeed increment per id change with the yaw rotated across the whole target ring. The Single mode at the default 10-15 CPS bounds keeps avgtime around 66-100ms per hit, under the 150ms threshold. The 1.9+ click-delay mode lowers the rate for swords (1/speed*20-1 ticks = about 11.5 ticks between hits, near the 150ms boundary) but the Snap and Autistic AntiCheat rotation modes blow past the 50-degree average-yaw ceiling: Snap snaps the full angle to the target each tick and Autistic AntiCheat rotates by rotationSpeed*10 continuously. Each signal accumulates its own partial violation and the module is cancelled once angleVL crosses the action thresholds.

countering.label: FightHitbox (ray trace to lag-compensated hitbox)
countering.explanation: Hawk's FightHitbox replays each attack from the packet-observed yaw/pitch. Because 1.8 sends the C02 before the yaw update, Hawk defers the ray trace to the next MoveEvent, then builds the direction from the stored yaw/pitch, rewinds the victim to its ping-ago position via the lag compensator, expands the victim AABB by 0.005, and ray-casts from the attacker eye (with the sneaking -0.08 offset and vehicle handling). No intersection punishes 'Did not hit hitbox.'; an intersection beyond MAX_REACH (3.1 survival, 5.0 creative) punishes as reach; with checkOccluding a BlockIterator flags hits through walls. KillAura's throughWalls mode is the direct target: when throughWalls is on (and rayCast off) the module expands the target's bounding box by 0.1 and attacks on any intercept, which is precisely the geometry Hawk re-derives from the server direction; the check's own epsilon and the lag-compensated victim position do not include the module's 0.1 expansion, so wall hits either miss the box entirely or exceed the reach limit. The Multiple mode attacking several entities in one tick fails the direction requirement for all but the one the look vector happens to cross. The module's rayCast-on mode (RayCastUtil.rayCast with -0.1f expansion) survives only when the server-observed rotations genuinely cross the rewound victim box within 3.1, which is the Legit/Normal rotation mode at default range.

countering.label: combat.KillAura (direction, multi, noswing, reach, speed)
countering.explanation: Arc's KillAura check runs from the FightListener on every C02 and combines five detectors. Direction computes the angle between the player's look direction and the vector to the attacked entity and flags over max-direction-angle; Multi compares the angles to the current and previous attacked entity and flags when the angle difference exceeds the limit while both entities are within maxReach of each other; NoSwing flags when maxSwingTime passes without an arm swing; Reach measures the distance to the entity minus its current velocity (so knockback does not false-flag) against maxReach; Speed counts attacks per second against maxAttacks and raw attack packets per second against maxAttackPackets via checkFrequency. KillAura's Multiple mode is the clean hit: attacking several entities in one tick means the single look vector can only satisfy the Direction check for one of them, and the angle difference between the attacked entities trips the Multi branch. The module's noSwing option (noSwing BooleanValue, default false) when enabled removes the C0A entirely, tripping NoSwing. The cps bounds up to 20 with the Normal click-delay mode exceed maxAttacks and maxAttackPackets per second. The Autistic AntiCheat rotation mode, which rotates yaw by rotationSpeed*10 per tick, is caught by the Direction angle since the look vector is usually far from the target when the attack fires.
